why_it_matters: Each pair is a single deliverable that the Step-2 prompt has to request exactly once. As written the generator is told to produce both 10 icon families and 20 icon sets, both 8 and 12 divider treatments plus 10 divider components, both 6 and 10 logo lockups. Whoever writes the prompt has to guess, and whoever writes the ingest validator cannot state the expected count in `token.capability-manifest` (§7.12), which is specified to carry "expected token count per group".
suggested_fix: For each overlapping pair, declare one owner (§7 item = the system-level spec; §8 row = the component that renders it) with a `renders:` / `specified-by:` cross-reference, and make the counts identical or explicitly explain the difference (e.g. "10 families, each family shipping a 6-lockup set").

missing: The three-tier budget is never actually applied. §8.2 says "Assign the tier at inventory time; the number then follows mechanically and the list cannot drift", and sizes the tiers as ~22 Tier A + ~90 Tier B + artwork. But no row in any §8.3 table carries a tier — the columns are Component | Variants | Priority | Rationale — and the totals do not reconcile: §8.3's tables enumerate ~215 component rows (Navigation 18, Hero 5, Content 32, Social proof 12, Commerce 13, Form 33, Feedback 23, Data display 27, Media 18, Utility 14, Page templates 20), the ARIA note in the same subsection says "~25 of ~240 items", and §8.2 accounts for only ~118. Tier B is therefore understated by roughly 80 items. §8 also has no per-row pickable/derived marking equivalent to §7's `derived` / `n/a` key — only four rows in the whole of §8 use one.
why_it_matters: The "cannot drift" guarantee is unverifiable, so the reviewer's literal check (is every item identity-carrying-and-picked or derived-and-not-picked, per D1?) cannot be run against §8 at all. It also means the count on any given row can be neither justified nor challenged: a reader cannot tell whether "Stat tile / KPI card 10" is 10 because it is Tier A, or 10 by accident.
suggested_fix: Add a Tier column (A/B/C) and a Pickable column (pick / computed / n-a) to every §8.3 row, then recompute the §8.2 tier sizes from the actual rows and correct the ~22/~90 figures and the ~240 total so the three numbers agree.

missing: Four components carry Priority **v1** in §8.3 but are absent from the §8.4 v1 set: Dropdown / flyout menu **7** (Navigation, v1), Radio group **8** (Form, v1), Toggle switch **8** (Form, v1), Platform CTA badge registry **5** (Commerce, v1). The list's own totals are also wrong: it claims "~50 pickable items, ~430 generated variants", but the enumerated list contains ~81 entries (~74 of them pickable items, the rest state sets and the state matrix), and summing the §8.3 counts for exactly the items it names gives 518 variants before any of the eleven §9 motion/art-container items (which add at least another ~60, e.g. background layer 10, section reveal 10, text reveal 10, custom cursor 10, marquee 6).
why_it_matters: §8.4 is the scope contract that §18's phasing and §13's render budget are built on, and §8.3's own line "~20 captures per selected variant" turns the variant total directly into a QA cost (430 → ~8,600 captures; 518+ → ~11,000+). A 20% item undercount and a 20%+ variant undercount silently under-scopes v1, and a form system shipping without a radio group or a toggle switch is a functional hole no reader would expect from a list headed "v1 set".
suggested_fix: Regenerate §8.4 mechanically from the Priority column rather than by hand, print the item count and the summed variant count with the arithmetic shown, and either add the four missing v1 items or change their Priority to v2 with a stated reason.

missing: Rows that state a number but give neither an enumeration of the N options nor any basis for N, so the count cannot be checked or built to: `shape.stroke-style-set` **4**, `effect.noise-grain` **8**, `effect.gradient-mesh` **8**, `shape.clip-and-mask-shapes` **10** (enumerates 8 then literally says "+ 2"), `cursor.personality` **6** (enumerates 4 kinds), `mark.decorative-glyphs` **10** (enumerates 8), `icon.family-spec` **10**, `mark.logo-lockups` **10** (enumerates 5 lockups), `system.voice-and-microcopy` **10**, `art.background-scene` **20**, `art.hero-artwork` **20**, `art.spot-illustrations` **20**, `art.avatar-style` **8** (enumerates 5), `art.3d-or-canvas-scene` **6**, `art.empty-state` **10**, `art.error-state` **10**. Separately, §8 (#Page templates) row "Team | **3** | v3" has a literally empty Rationale cell — the only wholly blank cell in either section.
why_it_matters: The user's stated completeness bar is that every item carries a suggested number of variants AND a rationale. These rows carry a number plus a rationale for the ITEM's existence, not for the number, and several enumerate fewer options than the number they claim. "+ 2" is an unresolved TBD inside a spec table. The Step-2 prompt generator has to emit a concrete request per item; for these rows it has nothing to say beyond "make 8 of them", which is exactly how undifferentiated variants (banned by §8.5's 200×120px rule) get produced.
suggested_fix: Enumerate every option for every numbered row in §7, exactly as §7.6 `shape.per-corner-recipes`, `shape.divider-treatment` and `effect.pattern-tiles` already do; resolve `shape.clip-and-mask-shapes`'s "+2"; fill the Team template rationale.

missing: §7 has no Priority column and no v1/v2/v3 cut list, while §8 has both. All 149 §7 items are therefore implicitly v1 and implicitly requested in the Step-2 prompt.
why_it_matters: §6.3 shows the Step-2 payload is context-bound ("~400KB / ~110K tokens against a 200K claude.ai context that artifacts count against") and §6.3's whole Stage-A/Stage-B design exists to avoid generating things nobody will use. Without a phase marking on §7, there is no way to say which of the 149 items must exist for the first shippable direction versus which can be generated on demand in Step 5, and no way to check the prompt against a budget. §18 can phase components but cannot phase the design system they consume.
suggested_fix: Add a Priority column to every §7 table using the same v1/v2/v3 vocabulary as §8, and add a §7.14 v1 cut list stating the item count, the expected resolved-token count, and which items are deferred to Step 5 regeneration.

missing: There is no container-query token family. §11.5 mandates `container-type: inline-size` on every block wrapper with component internals written in `@container`, and §19 A46 gates it — but §7.4 defines only viewport breakpoints (320/390/768/1280/1440) and viewport-relative container widths, and §8's states table calls that viewport set "The enforcement mechanism for D2". Nothing defines the container-size thresholds components switch at, their token names, or how they relate to `layout.grid-definition`'s column module.
why_it_matters: Under D2 a component is dragged into an arbitrary-width slot, so its internal layout switch has to key off container width, not viewport width — the PRD says so in §11.5 and then never supplies the values. An implementer writing a card's `@container` rules has no tokens to reference, and §7.12's `token.raw-value-lint` (raw-hex/px grep) would reject the literal px thresholds they would otherwise have to hard-code. The D2 acceptance criterion A46 ("moving a card from a 6-col to a 3-col slot requires no manual fix") is therefore untestable against any stated numbers.
suggested_fix: Add `layout.container-breakpoints` (n/a, shared across directions, e.g. narrow/medium/wide keyed to 3/6/12-column slot widths at the 1280 authoring breakpoint) and `layout.container-name-registry` to §7.4, cross-reference §11.5, and exempt those tokens explicitly from the raw-value lint.

section: 8 (#Feedback: Tooltip, Popover, Hover card; #Navigation: Dropdown / flyout, Mega menu) and 7 (no pointer-capability item)
missing: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (Level AA) is never named or gated. Tooltip **6** is called "a required companion to every icon button"; Popover **5**, Hover card **4** ("Desktop-only with no touch equivalent — must always degrade", with no statement of what "degrade" means), Dropdown / flyout **7** and Mega menu **6** are all hover/focus-triggered overlays. None carries the three 1.4.13 requirements (dismissable without moving the pointer, hoverable without disappearing, persistent until dismissed/invalid). §7 has no pointer- or hover-capability policy item either (`@media (hover: hover)` / `pointer: coarse`), and §8's state list has no hover-capability state.
why_it_matters: 1.4.13 is an AA criterion that direct manipulation makes worse, not better: a user can drag a tooltip-bearing icon button next to a viewport edge, and the resulting flip/reposition behaviour is exactly where dismissability and hoverability break. With 28 hover-triggered variants specified and no gate, a compliant implementation is a coincidence. It also leaves "must always degrade" unbuildable — on a coarse pointer, does the hover card open on tap, on long-press, or not at all?
suggested_fix: Add a 1.4.13 gate row to §13's quality gates covering all hover/focus overlay families, state the coarse-pointer behaviour per family in §8, and add a `interaction.pointer-capability-policy` n/a item to §7.4 defining hover/pointer media-query rules and the touch equivalent for every hover-only affordance.

section: 8 (#Media: Background video loop; #Social proof: Animated counter) versus 9 (Marquee / ticker)
missing: WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (Level A) is gated in §9 for the marquee ("WCAG 2.2.2 pause/hide is mandatory") and via APG for Testimonial carousel, but not for §8's auto-moving components: "Background video loop **5** — Loop engineering and a 4–16s cap constrain all five" (auto-playing motion longer than 5s with no stated pause/stop control) and "Animated counter **6** — Must ship a reduced-motion static variant" (reduced-motion is a different requirement from a user-operable pause).
why_it_matters: 2.2.2 is Level A, not AA — it is the floor. A 4–16s auto-looping background video is precisely the case the criterion was written for, and `prefers-reduced-motion` does not satisfy it because it is an OS preference, not a mechanism on the page. Two of the rows most likely to appear on the hero (the highest-surface component in the PRD) ship with no pause affordance in their variant definitions.
suggested_fix: Add the 2.2.2 requirement to the Background video loop and Animated counter rows (and any other auto-starting motion in §8), with the control's placement and its own contrast/target-size requirements, and add a single 2.2.2 coverage check to the lock-time gates that enumerates every auto-moving component on the page.

section: 8.3 (ARIA note) and every unmarked interactive row
missing: §8.3 states that [APG] items' "variants are skin-only; behaviour comes from a single audited implementation, identical across all variants", and that ~25 of ~240 items qualify. It never says where behaviour comes from for interactive components that are NOT marked [APG]: Mega menu panel 6, Command palette 4, Search overlay + results dropdown 6, Mobile drawer 10, Drawer / sheet 6, Cart drawer 4, Popover 5, Hover card 4, Toast / snackbar 6, Inline alert 6, Announcement / promo bar 8 (dismissal), Cookie / consent banner 6 (focus management), Cookie preferences centre 3, Search input control 6, File upload / dropzone 6, Date picker 5, Rating input 4, Removable chip 6.
why_it_matters: Those 18 rows total ~100 variants of components with real keyboard, focus-trap and live-region contracts — a drawer needs the same focus trap and Escape handling as a modal; a toast needs `role="status"`/`aria-live`; an announcement bar dismissal is the APG Disclosure pattern; a mega menu is Menubar/Disclosure. By the section's own logic (behaviour is centralised only for [APG] items), each of these gets its behaviour re-invented per skin. That is both an implementability hole (no named source of truth) and a WCAG 2.1.1/2.1.2/4.1.3 exposure across the most-used components on the site.
suggested_fix: Either extend the [APG] marking to every row with a keyboard/focus/live-region contract (mapping each to its APG pattern or to a named audited primitive), or add a third marking, e.g. [BEH], meaning "behaviour from a shared audited primitive, skin-only variants", and state which primitive.

missing: The state coverage list omits three states it needs: (1) `prefers-contrast: more` — §7.2 generates "a third solve at an elevated contrast multiplier via `prefers-contrast: more`", but the Theme state set is only "light / dark / forced-colors", so the third solve is never rendered, captured or verified anywhere; (2) WCAG 1.4.12 Text Spacing (Level AA) — no user-text-spacing-override state, despite fluid type, computed `size.control-heights` and drag-positioned blocks all being clipping candidates; (3) a pointer/hover-capability state (`hover: none`, `pointer: coarse`), needed by every hover-triggered row in §8 and by the custom cursor.
why_it_matters: §8's own framing is that this table "supplies the COVERAGE" and that "missing states are the most common completeness failure in generated systems". A generated-but-never-rendered high-contrast scheme is worse than none, because §13's proof tables will report the direction as compliant while nobody has ever looked at that scheme. 1.4.12 is a Level AA criterion that direct manipulation of fixed-height, tightly-packed blocks reliably breaks.
suggested_fix: Add the three states to the §8 state table with their render conditions, and update the "~20 captures per selected variant" arithmetic (5 breakpoints × 2 themes × 2 motion) to account for the added render axes or state explicitly which are spot-checked rather than swept.

missing: Two rules stated as hard requirements are unmeasurable as written. (1) "Hard rule: if two variants are indistinguishable at 200×120px, one must be regenerated or deleted" — no definition of indistinguishable: no perceptual-diff algorithm, no threshold, no judge (human or automated), no statement of which render conditions (theme, breakpoint, copy) the comparison uses. (2) "Sort by structural distance from the current pick" — "structural distance" is never defined, yet it is the mitigation assigned to the set-complexity moderator and the basis of the claim that a feature-sorted grid scans in near-constant time. "Label the differing axis" likewise assumes a variant schema with named axes that §8 never specifies.
why_it_matters: §8.5 is the argument that 10 variants is safe; §20.2 #2 records that the whole 10-variant decision rests on the four moderators being "engineerable away". If the two engineering fixes cannot be implemented or tested, the safety argument is unsupported and the 200×120px rule cannot be enforced at generation time — meaning the failure mode the section itself identifies (undifferentiated options) has no gate. §20.1 also excludes the VLM aesthetic judge, so there is no obvious existing mechanism to fall back on.
suggested_fix: Define structural distance concretely (e.g. Hamming distance over a declared per-component axis vector such as media-side / column-count / alignment / density / framing, which also gives "label the differing axis" its data), and define indistinguishability as a numeric threshold on a named metric (e.g. SSIM or CIEDE2000-weighted pixel diff over the 200×120 thumbnail in both themes) with the pass/fail value stated.

missing: Three form items that a complete builder vocabulary requires: (1) an error-summary block (the list of errors at the top of a failed form, linking to each field) — the inventory has "Field group (label / help / error) 6" for per-field errors only, and "Contact form 6 — needs designed success/error/submitting" without saying what the form-level error presentation is; (2) a required-field indicator policy (asterisk vs "optional" labelling, and its accessible name consequence); (3) an `autocomplete` attribute mapping for WCAG 2.2 SC 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (Level AA) — `autocomplete` appears exactly once in §8, as `one-time-code` on the OTP row.
why_it_matters: 1.3.5 is a Level AA criterion that applies to every field collecting the user's own data, which is every contact form and newsletter block in the v1 cut list; it is satisfied only by attributes nobody will add unless the inventory says so. The error summary is the standard remediation for 3.3.1/3.3.3 on multi-field forms and is the one form surface a design system must art-direct because it appears at the top of the page after a failed submit.
suggested_fix: Add "Form error summary 4" and "Required/optional indicator policy (n/a, policy)" rows to §8 #Form, and add an `autocomplete` token/mapping item to §7 (or a policy row in §8) covering the standard field-purpose list.

missing: No non-text-alternative requirement for charts. §8 specifies 12 chart marks plus Sparkline 4 and Chart chrome kit 4, and §7.11 covers only colour (categorical, sequential, diverging, structural tokens). Nothing requires each chart variant to ship an accessible alternative — a data table, a text summary, or `role="img"` with a meaningful accessible name — and nothing requires the underlying data to survive to the exported static site at LOCK. §7.10's `system.alt-text-policy` covers artwork records, not generated charts.
why_it_matters: WCAG 1.1.1 is Level A. Charts are non-text content by definition, and §20.1 puts v1 charts on a build-time SVG path, meaning the accessible alternative has to be emitted at build time or it does not exist at all. The user explicitly named graphs and charts as custom components they intend to add (vision step 6), so this is a named feature shipping without its Level A floor.
suggested_fix: Add a chart accessibility contract row to §8 #Data display (accessible name + description, visually-hidden data table or summary, and a rule that the delta/series distinction is never colour-only, matching the existing stat-tile and status-dot rules), and gate it at LOCK.

missing: The `color-scheme` CSS property is still absent. Five of the six "invisible surfaces" flagged in the recorded §7 gap were added (`color.scrollbar`, `color.caret`, `color.accent-color`, `color.selection`, `color.forced-colors-mapping`), but `color-scheme: light dark` — the declaration that tells the UA which scheme is in use and drives native form-control rendering, the default scrollbar, and `light-dark()` — has no row.
why_it_matters: It is the token the other five depend on: `accent-color` on native controls and any `scrollbar-color: auto` fallback resolve against the UA scheme, and without `color-scheme` a dark direction renders light native selects, date pickers and scrollbars — the exact one-second amateur tell the other five rows were added to prevent. It is also the enabling declaration for `light-dark()`, which §7.2's per-scheme values would otherwise have to duplicate by hand.
suggested_fix: Add `color.scheme-declaration` (derived, pickable:false) to §7.2 specifying the root `color-scheme` value per scheme strategy, its interaction with `color.accent-color` and `color.scrollbar`, and whether `light-dark()` is the emitted form.

missing: The category letters skip two values: A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, then L, then N, O. Categories K and M do not appear in §7, are not referenced anywhere else in the PRD, and are not listed in §20.1's deliberate-exclusions table.
why_it_matters: §20.1 exists precisely so that dropped items are traded, not lost, and the PRD's completeness claim rests on it. Two missing letters in a lettered scheme is direct evidence that two categories were cut during editing without passing through the exclusions table, and a reader has no way to determine what they contained. Candidate families with no home anywhere in §7 — internationalisation/localisation beyond `type.script-and-rtl-coverage`, SEO/metadata beyond favicon and OG, and sound/sonic identity (despite §8 shipping a Sound toggle and an Audio player) — are consistent with something having been dropped.
suggested_fix: Either restore K and M, or re-letter A–M contiguously and add a line to §20.1 recording what K and M were and why they were dropped.

missing: The heading claims a "26-slot identity vector" and the table has 26 rows, but two of them are marked `n/a` and are explicitly invariant across directions: `direction.reference-triangulation` (provenance metadata) and `type.viewport-endpoints` ("Must be identical across all directions"). Only 24 slots can actually vary. `token.direction-hash` specifies `{id, vectorHash}` with "Builder rejects mismatches" but never states which slots feed the hash, in what order, or how a value like a 40–80 word manifesto is canonicalised before hashing.
why_it_matters: §6.2's chunk envelope and §7.12's builder rejection both key off the vector and its hash, and §6.3's Chunk A is defined as "~10 direction capsules (26-slot vector + manifesto)". If two implementations disagree on whether the invariant rows are in the hash — or on manifesto normalisation (whitespace, unicode, casing) — every ingest fails the mismatch check for a reason no error message will explain.
suggested_fix: State the vector as 24 varying slots plus 2 invariant records, and specify the hash input precisely: the ordered slot list, the canonical serialisation, and the hash function.

missing: The component-bar spec covers only the 10-variant case: "5 thumbnails visible in the strip, arrow/scroll to reach all 10", "skeleton filter chips above 12 items", "Compare 3", "More like this generates 5 neighbours and appends them". It does not cover the six 12-variant Tier-A components (hero, feature grid, card, CTA band, pricing, badge) which sit exactly at the filter-chip boundary, the 20-item artwork sets (icon set, illustration set, spot graphics, patterns, and §7.9's 20-piece background/hero artwork), or what the strip looks like after "More like this" has appended 5 (10 → 15, or 20 → 25).
why_it_matters: Artwork is the tier the user is most likely to browse (D1's "20 artworks tagged by direction"), and it is the one case the presentation spec never addresses — 20 items with filter chips, a 5-wide strip and an append action is a different interaction from a 10-item strip. Without it the editor's most-used panel is unspecified for its largest sets, and the choice-overload argument in the same subsection was only made for 10.
suggested_fix: Extend the presentation spec to state the strip behaviour, filter-chip trigger and grid fallback for 12-, 20- and post-append set sizes, and say whether artwork uses a filtered grid (as §8 #Media's "parallel-scannable as a filtered grid" implies) rather than the strip.
